intended_object: The open half-plane {(x, z) : x > -1}, packaged as a `ProfileHistories.RadialDomain`, i.e. a domain closed under the contractions (x, z) ↦ (t·x, z) for t ∈ [0,1]. The docstring describes it as a device: after shifting the radial variable by one, an "anchored integral" becomes a standard radial history on this domain.
explanation:
`RadialDomain` is a structure specific to this library. It bundles an open set in `Point` (the plane ℝ×ℝ) with the property that scaling the first coordinate by any t ∈ [0,1] keeps points inside. The definition is one instance of it: the carrier is {p | -1 < p.1}. It is open (`isOpen_lt`), and it is stable under the scaling: if p.1 ≥ 0 then t·p.1 ≥ 0 > -1, and if p.1 < 0 then t·p.1 ≥ p.1 > -1. So the bundled set really is the half-plane x > -1, and the proofs are sound.

The definition does not formalize a standard notion from the literature. As its docstring says, it exists so that a translated radial integral fits the library's own `RadialDomain` interface. That makes it an auxiliary construction for a proof, with no Mathlib counterpart. If it were instead read as "the half-plane x > -1", it would be a correct specific object.
